target_customer: Contractors building solar farms and data centers
problem: Infrastructure builds face labor shortages and robots struggle with high mix work. Libra builds AI that engineers robots for new tasks and sells completed work as a service.
business_model: Robots as a service, contractors pay for completed work (pay per watt reported for solar)

founders.name: Jermaine Zhao
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built robots in industrial automation, agriculture and utility scale solar; employers not named.

founders.name: Yaojing Huang
education: Stanford, civil engineering and computer science, PhD dissertation on construction robotics
founders.background_notes: Research at Stanford CIFE and Robotics Center; worked with 40+ contractors per the YC page.

competitors.name: AES Maximo
competitors.what: AI enabled robot installing solar modules
competitors.traction_then: 100 MW installed at the Bellefield complex (reported March 2026)

competitors.name: Cosmic Robotics
competitors.what: Robots to speed solar deployment for data centers

technical_complexity.rationale: Field deployable robots across embodiments on real construction sites require hardware, perception and manipulation work that two founders must scale.

defensibility.rationale: Multi embodiment AI and field data could compound, but funded competitors already install solar panels with robots.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors kept raising in 2025 and 2026; no acquisition of Libra found.

market_need_then: Solar and data center build outs face labor shortages; AES framed Maximo as installing at half the cost, and Planted Solar raised $31.8M to build solar for data centers with robots.

branding.domain_note: Uses librabots.com rather than libra.com or similar.

identity.logo: A logo and brand color are on Brandfetch; no design description
identity.voice_and_tone: Infrastructure and productivity framing, sells completed work not robots

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; the name is shared with unrelated Libra and Liberty companies.

outcome_analysis: Libra Robotics is a Fall 2026 company (a Fondo post calls it Summer 2026, a conflict) with robots on solar sites and data center pilots. Strong robotics founders fit the problem, but capital intensity and funded rivals are the main risks. No outcome yet.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed with no date or investors, one aggregator only, so no round is recorded. The directory batch is Fall 2026; a Fondo post dated 2026-10-16 says Summer 2026. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition. Competitor dates are approximate; Terabase date not shown. Undated competitor sources omitted from the list: Terabase Energy. Completeness pass: the $125K seed is recorded from Dealroom (single database, no date or investors, profile marked as AI made).
